findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Smeval.lean:290 `theorem smeval_commute_left (hc : Commute x y) : Commute (p.smeval x) y` — proved by `induction_on'` with `Commute.add_left` / `Commute.smul_left (Commute.pow_left ..)`, matching Semiconj.lean:58-62. Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Smeval.lean:295 `smeval_commute (hc : Commute x y) : Commute (p.smeval x) (q.smeval y)`, proved with an inner `induction n`.
findings.fix: Name `Polynomial.smeval_commute_left` instead of `Polynomial.smeval_commute`; if the proof-provenance remark is kept, keep it to that one lemma.
findings.issue: Docstring claims the lemma "generalizes Mathlib's `Polynomial.smeval_commute` from `Commute` to `SemiconjBy`, following its proof". `smeval_commute` evaluates two different polynomials (`Commute (p.smeval x) (q.smeval y)`) and is proved by a nested induction on the exponent; `smeval_right` uses one polynomial on both sides and does not imply it. The actual analogue it generalizes, and whose proof it follows, is `Polynomial.smeval_commute_left`.

findings.evidence: Commutation.lean:47-50 hypothesis `h : a * x = x * (a + c)`, conclusion `... * Ring.choose (a + n • c) m`; TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/Semiconj.lean:76 calls `c` "the additive shift".
findings.fix: Say "by `n • c`" (or "by `n` copies of the shift `c`" / "`-n • c`"), matching Semiconj.lean's own wording "the additive shift `c`".
findings.issue: Docstring says the argument is shifted "by the accumulated commutator", but the shift is `n • c`, and `c` is not the commutator: from `h : a * x = x * (a + c)` one gets `⁅a, x⁆ = a*x - x*a = x * c`. Same wording at line 54 ("the negative accumulated commutator"). These are the only descriptions of the shift — neither docstring names `c`.

summary: Module docs and most declaration docstrings are accurate and honest about scope, but `SemiconjBy.smeval_right` cites the wrong Mathlib lemma as the result it generalizes, and both divided-power reordering lemmas describe the shift `n • c` as "the commutator", which it is not.
